name: Hidden Door Sensor
description: A wireless, battery-powered sensor recessed into a door frame that reports when the door opens or closes. It can trigger lights and other Insteon devices.

steps.text: Remove the battery isolation tab before first use.
Hold the sensor in its intended spot and try linking it to the Hub or a responder to test the location; if linking fails, reposition it or add a Range Extender.
Do all linking now, because installing the sensor covers its SET button.
Choose a spot on the hinge side of the door frame or of the door itself; higher is better for range.
Protect nearby surfaces with masking tape and drill a hole 4 inches deep and 3/4 inch in diameter.
Clean out the shavings, test the fit, then insert the sensor and fasten it with the included screw.
If the gap between door and frame is too wide to press the contact plunger, slide the spacer over the sensor and fasten it with the provided screw.

notes: Tools: power drill, 3/4-inch spade or auger bit, Phillips screwdriver. Uses one AAA battery.
It also works in casement window frames; for sash windows the manual recommends Open/Close Sensor 2843.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps.

notes: The first device put into linking mode becomes the controller and the second the responder. Linking mode ends once a link is made.
To control a device: adjust it to the state you want, then press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps.

When already installed (five-tap linking): with the door open, press and release the contact plunger twice, then hold it until the sensor beeps; or with the door closed, open it and press and release the plunger twice, and after a pause the sensor beeps. Repeating five-tap linking cycles between linking, unlinking and exit; the door can be opened or closed while in linking mode.
To add it to a Hub, when the app prompts, press and hold the SET button until the sensor beeps.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps, then tap the SET button.
Adjust each scene member to its state and, one at a time, press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button once to finish the scene.

notes: Multi-linking mode lasts 4 minutes or until the SET button is tapped.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps.

notes: Then press and hold the controlled device's SET button until it double-beeps.

For several devices, tap the SET button after the second beep, press and hold each device's SET button until it double-beeps, then tap the SET button to leave multi-unlinking mode (it also ends after 4 minutes).

steps.text: While the sensor is awake, send Set Operating Flags with cmd2 0x18 (stay awake on) to keep it awake; cmd2 0x19 turns it off.

notes: The Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes say the sensor sleeps quickly to save battery and must be awake to receive commands; stay awake on uses 0xFF for the awake interval.
The documents don't give a button step to wake the sensor before sending the command.

verification.note: Only the Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes cover staying awake.

steps.text: Remove the Hidden Door Sensor from the door frame and take out its battery.
Press and hold the SET button while reinstalling the battery.
Keep holding the SET button until the long beep stops, then let go.

notes: Erases all links and customized properties.
Sends closed to group 2 only when set to.
Sends a heartbeat to group 4 every 24 hours by default. Software can set it to 5 to 1275 minutes, in 5-minute steps.
Sends low battery to group 3 each time it wakes while its battery is below a level software sets.
Sends low battery and heartbeat only when it has links in those groups.
Its heartbeat and low battery messages carry cmd1 0x11 while the door is open and 0x13 while it's closed.
Its Developer Notes give the heartbeat as every 24 hours by default; other sources give 256 times 5 minutes, about 21 hours.
Its owner's manual says the sensor sends its heartbeat once every 24 hours by default.
